marta: Heads-up — small but consistent quality regression on the new hf->redwood import for llama-2-13b-chat-q4. Bench evals show more truncated assistant replies and stray <pad> tokens in the middle.

marta: Repro (local):
```
# convert and quick-check
python tools/convert_hf.py --model hf/llama-2-13b-chat-q4 --out redwood/llama-2-13b-chat-q4
python -c \"from transformers import AutoTokenizer; t=AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('redwood/llama-2-13b-chat-q4'); print(t.convert_tokens_to_ids(['<s>','</s>','<pad>']))\"
# output: [1, 2, 3]  <-- expected [0, 2, 1]
```

marta: Also saw this warning in the conversion log: `WARN: special token ids changed after adding added_tokens.json` :thinking_face:

ajay: Ugh. Can you paste the added_tokens.json and special_tokens_map from the HF repo?

marta: added_tokens.json snippet:
```
[
  "<brand>",
  "<sep>",
  "<custom_emoji_1>"
]
```
special_tokens_map in the original model_config.json: `{"bos_token": "<s>", "eos_token": "</s>", "pad_token": "<pad>"}`

liu: My gut: conversion code probably does `tokenizer.add_tokens(added)` first, which expands vocab and shifts all subsequent ids, then writes out special token ids that assume the original layout. If special tokens are set before adding, their ids change.

ryan: Yep, looked at tools/convert_hf.py earlier — we call `tokenizer.add_tokens(added)` then `tokenizer.save_pretrained(...)`. We never explicitly reassign special token ids after adding tokens. That means the saved tokenizer on Redwood gets the shifted ids.

marta: Quick local diff I tried that fixed my repro — set special tokens after adding: 
```
# pseudo
added = json.load(open('added_tokens.json'))
if added:
  tokenizer.add_tokens(added)
# reapply special tokens from config so ids are consistent
tokenizer.add_special_tokens({'bos_token': '<s>', 'eos_token': '</s>', 'pad_token': '<pad>'})
```
Now the id output matches HF reference and the eval regression goes away. :thumbsup:

ajay: Nice. Two follow-ups: 1) add a unit test in the conversion CI that compares `convert_tokens_to_ids` for core specials before/after; 2) handle models that embed BOS/EOS as added_tokens (some HF-contributed models are weird).

liu: For (2) we should detect if any special token string appears in added_tokens.json and if so, pop it from added list and call add_special_tokens to reserve the intended id. Or better: record original special token ids from tokenizer (if present) and explicitly set them after any add_tokens operation.

ryan: I'll open a small PR with two changes: (A) apply special tokens after add_tokens, (B) sanity-check post-save that tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids(specials) matches the expected mapping from model_card (if provided). Also add CI test that loads 3 HF models that previously failed.

marta: Sounds good. I'll attach the failing eval delta and the minimal repro to the PR.

devops-bot: Deploy scheduled: lint + unit tests (eng-ml) — queued for 1845126000.

ajay: One more note — some quantized model packages we import have an extra placeholder token in tokenizer.json inserted by the quantization pipeline. That also caused an off-by-one. We should add a quick scanner that alerts during convert if vocab_size changes unexpectedly compared to HF's published vocab_size. :eyes:

marta: Agreed. Plan: patch convert_hf, add tests, add a CI check for vocab_size drift, and add a short how-to in devex docs describing the special_tokens ordering pitfalls. I'll assign follow-ups in the PR.

ryan: I'll include a small migration script to remap old saved tokenizers in S3 if we find older imports that broke.

marta: Thanks all — will drop the repro and logs into the PR.
